scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports. Known source-confirmed gaps only, not an exhaustive acceptance claim.

findings.finding: A query, INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE is checked over the visit infos of the build that plans it (`table_privilege::check_plan_privilege`: a query's before it is optimized, a DML's once it is built, a point plan's through `check_fast_plan_privilege`). PREPARE, the binary protocol's prepare and a new non-prepared plan-cache entry keep the `VisitInfos` of one build (`Session::collect_table_privileges`), as Go's `GeneratePlanCacheStmtWithAST` keeps those of its `destBuilder.Build`: a query's is `query_visit_info`'s `build_query_node`, a DML's is the driver's own build with no fast plan (`dml_visit_info`). What remains: that DML build is a second one beside the plan the prepare caches (`build_prepared_dml_plan`), where Go builds once; and an INSERT's visit infos come from the separate builders of its target, source and values, where Go's `buildInsert` has one `PlanBuilder`

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: `FlashbackCluster` runs (`cluster_ddl/flashback_cluster.rs` is Go's `pkg/ddl/cluster.go`, `tidb-domain-infosync` `schedule_manager.rs` its PD schedule), with one difference left (the region RPC loops and the GC safe point refusal run against a real TiKV in `rust/scripts/run-realtikv-flashback-cluster.sh`, outside the gate; the warning for a gap between local time and PD's TSO has no test here or in Go): the node tests end a job step at `beforeRunOneJobStep` where Go's use `afterWaitSchemaSynced`. The masking policies run (`tidb-session/src/masking_policy.rs` is the executor half, `cluster_ddl/masking_policy.rs` the worker's handlers and the hooks of DROP / TRUNCATE / RENAME TABLE, DROP DATABASE, DROP / MODIFY / CHANGE COLUMN), with two differences left: Go's infoschema loads `mysql.tidb_masking_policy` lazily into `MaskingPolicyByTableColumn` and the session reads the table for each statement instead, so it does not reproduce Go answering `masking policy p doesn't exist` after a reorganizing MODIFY / CHANGE COLUMN (Go keeps the policy cached under the old column ID although the row follows the column); and the hooks' tolerance of a missing table outside `StartMode` Normal has no test. `RepairTable` runs (`cluster_ddl/repair_table.rs`, the preprocessor's `handleRepairName` / `checkNotInRepair`, the loader's `repairFetchCreateTable` failpoint), with three differences left: the full load's repair-list filter (`issyncer` `load_info_schema`) has no test; `RepairInfo.CheckAndFetchRepairedTable` replaces a table already recorded, because the DDL worker's `LoadWithTS` and the domain's reload both apply a diff where Go's one `Loader` applies it once; and when a repair leaves two tables with one lowercased name (Go's repair checks no name) `table_info_by_name` answers the first listed where Go's name map answers the one applied last. `AlterTableMode` and `RefreshMeta` queue and run their jobs (`cluster_ddl/table_mode.rs`), and a table not in `TableModeNormal` is protected as Go's `core.CheckTableMode`, the foreign-key cascade's child check and the DDL executor's DROP TABLE / rename checks protect it (`ErrProtectedTableMode`); left out: internal SQL sessions that compile without the statement's resolved names, a prepared DDL's `inPrepare` names, Go's skip on a plan-cache hit, and LOAD DATA / IMPORT INTO, which no test covers. Every other statement builds its job in `build_ddl_job` (Go's executor method up to `DoDDLJobWrapper`) and submits it through `RealClusterDdl::do_ddl_job_wrapper`, though still lowered into this port's own `DdlStatement` (`cluster_ddl.rs` `lower_ddl_with_context`) rather than one method per statement

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: No ingest (fast-reorg) backfill: it falls back to the transactional merge (`tidb-ddl/src/cluster_ddl/add_index.rs`); with it the status port's `/ingest/*` routes (Go `IngestConcurrencyHandler` over `ingestctrl`'s rate-limit parameters) are absent, and so is the DXF add-index task's `autoPauseAddIndexJobOnKVDiskFull`, the one producer of the system pause a multi-schema change promotes (`promote_proxy_kv_disk_full_pause`); the DXF backfill executor's Top SQL attach (`attachTopProfilingInfo` in `backfilling_dist_executor.go`) goes with it

Root HashAgg is Go's `HashAggExec` (`tidb-executor-aggregate/src/agg_hash_executor.rs`: fetcher, partial workers shuffling one mapper per final worker, final workers, `parallelHashAggSpillHelper` spill), and its serial and parallel memory are Go's to the byte for global and pushed-down aggregates (`sum(a)` 12.6 KB, `b, count(a) ... group by b` 13.5 KB, `count(distinct b)` 12.4 KB) (a grouped scan-fed `a, group_concat(b) ... group by a` 14.0 KB and an index-fed `count(distinct a)` 12.3 KB, as a Go statement loop that installs the connection's allocator charges them); its disk tracker exists only where Go's `initForUnparallelExec` / `initForParallelExec` create one (a distinct aggregate's EXPLAIN ANALYZE disk is `N/A`); its fetcher's capacity-0 input chunks fill through the select result's Go `Decoder` (`Decode` appends each buffer once and rounds its rows up to eight; `ReuseIntermChk` swaps a large remainder in), so a four-row VARCHAR-keyed response grows its input chunk by Go's 96 bytes (offsets 5/6) and `b, count(a) ... group by b`'s HashAgg peaks at Go's 13801 bytes; after earlier statements on one connection the workers' chunks receive the same recycled columns Go's do, so the charge follows the connection's history as Go's does (over a server connection the group_concat run after a `count(distinct a)` charges Go's 18.0 KB, the `b, count(a)` after it Go's 16.9 KB; an in-process session matches Go's allocator with an unpooled result chunk, 14.8 KB and 14.2 KB); a cop-side aggregation with no pushed form (`pushed_partial_aggregation` refuses its function kind, or an argument the pushdown catalog cannot lower: X01) runs in this tier on Go's TiDB-tier `HashAggExec` / `StreamAggExec`, where Go always runs it in the coprocessor; in the suites and the corpus only a TiFlash fragment's aggregates (M01) reach it

`IndexLookUpExecutor`'s memory and RU v2 are Go's, on every run: the double read (`IndexRangeSourceExec`, `access_path.rs` `IndexLookUpMemory`) owns a tracker labelled with its plan that each open attaches to the statement's, charged with its index ranges' KV ranges (`buildTableKeyRanges`), the index worker's responses (`LabelForIndexWorker`) and each table task's `executeTask` bytes (`cap(handles)` and the handles, the task's `TableReaderExecutor` at 768 plus its KV ranges and `dagPB.Size()`, the chunks it fills, `task.rows`, a keep-order `indexOrder` and `rowIdx`), the next task releasing the last; each task's reader records `TableReaderExecutor` into the parent's accumulator. EXPLAIN ANALYZE and `tidb_mem_quota_query` match Go for integer, keep-order `_tidb_rowid` and clustered handles (`tests_explain.rs` `an_index_lookup_charges_its_tasks_like_go`). The index worker's fetch chunk (`prepareHandleFetch`, typed by `getRetTpsForIndexReader`), each task reader's chunks (`TryNewCacheChunk`) and a serial projection's child chunk come from the session's allocator, so a task's charge follows the columns earlier statements returned to it, as Go's does (`an_index_lookup_takes_its_chunks_from_the_session_allocator_like_go`: `SELECT b, c FROM t USE INDEX(b) WHERE b > 1` charges 6.83 KB on a connection's first run and 14.1 KB after). A query's EXPLAIN ANALYZE result is written through a chunk taken from the allocator after the analyzed tree opens and before it runs (Go `ExplainExec`), and a pushed partial aggregate's tasks and a root `LimitExec` draw from it too, so a connection's statements reuse each other's columns as Go's do (`pipeline_mysql_client_source.rs` `a_connections_statements_reuse_each_others_chunks_like_go`). Under a pushed index-side Limit the index stream closes once the Limit is exhausted, before the task's reader charges it, as Go's index worker closes its result (`... LIMIT 64` 4.70 KB, `LIMIT 20` 2.47 KB: `an_index_lookup_under_a_pushed_limit_releases_its_index_response_like_go`). Remaining: the fetch chunk leaves out a keep-order merge's `byItems`; a task is exactly one `extractTaskHandles` batch (a whole 32-row response chunk through `ReuseIntermChk`), a table plan's Limit rides each task's request, a local index's partitioned task reads its rows without handles, and the table workers count every task they execute (`an_index_lookup_takes_one_response_chunk_per_task_like_go`); a task's reader takes its chunk before it blocks on the response, as Go's `TryNewCacheChunk` before `Next` does (`SELECT b, c FROM p USE INDEX(b) WHERE b > 90` over two partitions after a plain run charges 12.3 KB, one of the two values Go's racing index and table workers give: 4.45 KB or 12.3 KB, about evenly over eight runs); an unordered partitioned lookup over a local index reads each partition's index remotely, one partition's request at a time, and cuts its tasks at that partition's response chunks (`a_partitioned_index_lookup_reads_each_partitions_index_remotely_like_go`: Go's 4 tasks); a keep-order, global-index or dirty partitioned lookup's index side is still this port's native walk; a global index's unordered lookup reads its index remotely under the logical table, its request ending with `ExtraPhysTblID` and its handles Go's `kv.PartitionHandle`s (`needPartitionHandle`), so its tasks span partitions and are cut at the response chunks (`a_global_index_lookups_task_spans_partitions_like_go`; `a_global_index_lookup_cuts_its_tasks_at_response_chunks_like_go`: Go's 4 tasks at `tidb_index_lookup_size = 2`), and a read narrowed to some partitions sends Go's `in(_tidb_tid, ...)` Selection in its index request (`AddSelectionConditionForGlobalIndex`; `a_narrowed_global_index_lookup_filters_its_entries_in_the_store_like_go`, its index side counting each `idxResult.Next` as Go's does), and a keep-order one reads its index in order the same way (`a_keep_order_global_index_lookup_reads_its_index_remotely_like_go`), each task's one table request returning `ExtraPhysTblID`, by which its keep-order worker matches each row to its partition handle as Go's does; at the default lookup size a plain `SELECT * FROM t USE INDEX(ub) WHERE b > 1` peaks at 19,440 bytes where Go's peaks at 18,960, and its `ORDER BY b` at 50,686 where Go's peaks at 57,614 (its table worker's chunks come from the allocator at 896 and 8,192 bytes), neither yet traced tracker by tracker; a dirty global lookup still walks natively, as does a full read of a table adding or dropping partitions (Go's plan carries the `_tidb_tid` Selection there too, this port's does not), each task is one table reader whose one request spans its partitions (`SetPartitionsAndHandles`), unpaged as Go's lookup table reader is, so its region tasks are store-batched as Go's are (8 cop tasks in 4 RPCs, `store_batch_num: 4`, RU 2.38; the statement 23.3 KB where Go's racing workers give 20.5 to 23.2 KB); a task's table-side partial aggregate is pushed for integer, clustered and partitioned tables alike (`tests_slow_log.rs` `an_index_lookups_partial_aggregate_request_peaks_like_go`: each statement peak Go's to the byte); the index side reads its next handle batch as soon as it hands a task off, as Go's index worker does, so the response it drained is released before the task's reader charges (6 rows at `tidb_index_lookup_size` 2: Go's and this port's one 2.58 KB task, `an_index_lookup_releases_its_drained_index_response_before_the_task_like_go`; `p ... PARTITION BY HASH(a) PARTITIONS 2`, `b > 1`: both two tasks, 5.13 KB); a task the store answers without a table reader (`LookupFetch::LocalFallback`: a dirty transaction's read, a refused remote shape) charges nothing; and the reader is one source shared with `IndexReader` and index-merge partials, its tasks windows of one `LookupPipeline` over a `LanePool`, not Go's index worker, table workers and `resultCh`; an index join's inner lookup (`IndexJoinLookupExec`, built afresh per task on its inner worker as Go's `BuildExecutorForIndexJoin` builds it) charges and reports as Go's per-task `IndexLookUpExecutor` does (`an_index_join_charges_its_inner_index_lookup_like_go`, `an_index_joins_inner_lookups_register_their_stats_per_task_like_go`) without being one either

Every SQL read of TiKV and TiFlash is Go's reader: `TableReaderExecutor`, `IndexReaderExecutor`, `IndexLookUpExecutor` (a pushed-down lookup too: `buildIndexLookUpPushDownDAGReq`, its rows and handles split by channel as `extractLookUpPushDownRowsOrHandles`), `IndexMergeReaderExecutor` and `MPPGather` over Go's `ConstructDAGReq`; a union scan reads the buffer through Go's mem readers over every reader (`buildMemIndexMergeReader` and the `MPPGather` arm included), and an index join's inner side is Go's `dataReaderBuilder`. The in-process reader engine, its offer machinery and the probe-seeded index-join leaf are deleted (`docs/tikv-reader-execplan.md` M5). What still lowers a scan request instead of a plan (`cop_reader::build_resp` under `KvTableReader`'s row cursors) is the internal scans: ANALYZE's kv path (`analyze/kv.rs`), the privilege and account loads (`privilege_tables.rs`, `simple/account.rs`), partition maintenance (`kv_table/partition_maintenance.rs`) and TABLESAMPLE (`table_sample.rs`), where Go sends analyze requests, runs SQL over `mysql.*`, scans through the reorg backfill and samples with `tableRegionSampler`

The physical operators carry Go's fields (audit: `rust/scripts/physicalop-field-audit.py`; Go's flattened plan lists, which alias the reader's own tree, are borrowing views such as `PhysicalIndexLookUpReader::index_plans()`). Missing still: `PhysicalCTE.CTE` is the copied `CTEClass` fields, the session's `CTEClass` being `Rc<RefCell<_>>` logical state a cached physical plan cannot share; `PhysicalShuffleReceiverStub.Receiver`, the executor builder's pointer to its receiver, is the builder's (`shuffle::install_receivers`); a scan's `UsedStatsInfo` is read by EXPLAIN from the statement's used-stats map by physical table id, where Go keeps the entry's pointer. `PhysicalTableSample.TableInfo` comes with E15's TABLESAMPLE port (Go `tableRegionSampler`), `PhysicalCTESink` / `PhysicalCTESource` with M01's MPP CTE

A projection's vectorized result column takes the shape its Go builtin's `vecEval*` gives it (`chunk_executor.rs`: `Resize*`, `Reserve*` and appends, one argument evaluated into it, a column's `CopyReconstruct`) for arithmetic, comparisons and `IN`, logic, `NOT`/`IS NULL`/`IS TRUE`, casts, `IF`/`IFNULL`/`CASE`/`COALESCE`, `GREATEST`/`LEAST` (a string one ping-pongs `result` with two buffers, reserving it before its rows land), and every other builtin whose Go signature is `vectorized()` (`builtin_vec_result`: the math, time, JSON, info, string, bit, `LIKE`, encryption, miscellaneous, vector and variable builtins; `UUID`'s `ReserveStringWithSizeHint`), so a tree appends row by row exactly where Go's `evalOneColumn` does; a string `GREATEST`/`LEAST` shapes `result` as Go's kernels do (`Evaluator::run`'s `string_extremum_vec`: the direct signature's ping-pong appends a computed first argument's rows, then each even step's running value after a `ReserveString(n)`, and copies an even count's last step in by `CopyConstruct`; the compare-as-time signature evaluates every argument into `result` before its values), and a compare-as-time call is built as Go's is (its signature kept from the uncast arguments, every argument cast to a string, `doTimeConversionForGL`'s truncation and `checkMonthDay` warnings, a `strconv.Atoi` failure raised as 1105). The values still come from the row and batch evaluators rather than Go's `vecEval*` kernels, but under Go's `EvalExpr` choice (`vecEnabled && expr.Vectorized()`, scoped per projected expression and per filter; a Selection reads `tidb_enable_vectorized_expression` as Go's `SelectionExec` does) a string `GREATEST`/`LEAST` answers the later of two equal arguments as `vecEvalString` does, where a folded constant or a row evaluation keeps the earlier (`evalString`); a control function's row fallback (`fallbackEval*`, when a branch's vectorized evaluation warns) leaves the column the branch already sized and warns only for the branch a row takes (`a_control_function_warns_only_for_the_branch_a_row_takes_like_go`, the fallback rows of `a_projection_sizes_its_result_columns_as_go_vec_eval_does`)

The session's reusable chunk allocator is Go's (`Session::chunk_alloc`, Go `clientConn.chunkAlloc`: installed per statement as `NewSyncAllocator(alloc)` under `tidb_enable_reuse_chunk`, never for an internal `InRestrictedSQL` statement, reset between statements and recreated after a failed one, each statement's validity its own), executors take it as `ExecutorMeta::alloc_pool` (Go `AllocPool`) for `NewChunk` / `TryNewCacheChunk` / `NewChunkWithCapacity`, and Go's `NewFirstChunk` sites (`Executor::new_first_chunk`: projection workers, hash-join probe and result chunks, index-hash-join results, shuffle holders, the drained record set) allocate outside it, so memory charges match Go's in sequence (`a_projection_sizes_its_result_columns_as_go_vec_eval_does`, `explain_analyze_dml_roots_report_their_executor_stats_and_memory_like_go`). The connection writes a result through a chunk from the statement's allocator (`writeChunks`' `rs.NewChunk(GetChunkAllocator())`, `ResultSetSource::new_write_chunk`), and a covering `IndexReader` returns its `OutputColumns` from the source itself (`dagReq.OutputOffsets`) instead of through a projection's pooled chunk, so a later statement reuses the same columns Go's does: a point UPDATE's root charges Go's 638 / 889 Bytes / 1.11 KB over the wire after a point UPDATE, `select 1` or a scan (`pipeline_mysql_client_source.rs` `explain_for_connection_charges_reused_chunks_like_go`). An `INSERT ... SELECT` reads its source into a chunk from the statement's allocator taken once the source is open (Go `insertRowsFromSelect`'s `TryNewCacheChunk(selectExec)`), so the next statement reuses the columns it grew (`an_insert_select_returns_its_source_chunk_to_the_allocator_like_go`). A parallel projection's last answer swaps in the output its fetcher completed empty, and a Projection under a UnionAll copies its columns (`avoidColumnEvaluatorForProjBelowUnion`), as Go's do (`a_parallel_projection_swaps_in_its_last_output_like_go`). Remaining: executors built outside the physical builder's `meta` (`ExecutorMeta::new` in other crates and builder arms) allocate fresh; a materialized result (a plain EXPLAIN, SHOW and the other row-built statements) takes its write chunk from the allocator when its rows are already built (`a_plain_explain_and_a_show_write_through_pooled_chunks_like_go`, against the server binary), so a statement whose Go executor draws from the allocator before `Next` builds its rows (an EXPLAIN ANALYZE of a write, whose `ExplainExec` runs the write in `Next`) takes it after those draws; parallel apply's chunks, whose executor shape differs from Go's, are unmapped.
Lazy cursor fetch answers Go's `executor.Detach` over the physical plan (`tidb_executor::detach`), because the builder's operator tree is not Go's executor tree

No cross-keyspace runtime (null keyspace only); the next-gen-only surfaces built on it have no port either: the status port's `/dxf/*` and `/ddl/check/*`, the DXF framework's metering and `GetScheduleStatus` (`pkg/dxf/framework/metering`, `schstatus`), and plan replayer's `tidb_cloud_storage_uri` storage (`pkg/planner/extstore` `createGlobalExtStorage`, local files on a classic kernel)

An MPP reader runs as Go's `MPPGather` over Go's local coordinator (`tidb-executor` `mpp_gather.rs`, `local_mpp_coordinator.rs`): the planner's fragments (`GenerateRootMPPTasks`), each fragment's `ToPB` DAG dispatched to its tasks, the root tasks' packets received; the embedded store serves Go's MPP tasks, tunnels and exchange/join executors, and Go's `tiflashtest` tests pass on mock TiFlash stores (`TestMppExecution`, `TestReadUnsigedPK`, `TestJoinRace`, `TestInjectExtraProj`, `TestMppEnum`, `TestMppUnionAll`, `TestUnionWithEmptyDualTable`, `TestAvgOverflow`, `TestMppApply`, `TestTiFlashVirtualColumn`, `TestAggPushDownApplyAll`, `TestAggPushDownCountStar`, `TestIssue41014`, `TestMPP47766`, `TestAggPushDownUnionAndMPP`, `TestGroupStreamAggOnTiFlash`, `TestIssue50358`, `TestNonsupportCharsetTable`, `TestIssue57149`, `TestCanGenerateTiFlashCopWithKeepOrer`, `TestIssue59877`, `TestForbidTiFlashIfExtraPhysTableIDIsNeeded`, `TestIndexMergeCarePreferTiflash`, `TestTiFlashPlanCacheable`, `TestUnionScan`, `TestPartitionTable`, `TestMppAggShouldAlignFinalMode`, `TestIssue59703`, `TestDispatchTaskRetry`, `TestMppVersionError`, `TestMppStoreCntWithErrors`, `TestMPPMemoryTracker`, `TestCancelMppTasks`, `TestMppGoroutinesExitFromErrors`, `TestMPPRecovery`, `TestMppTableReaderCacheForSingleSQL`, `TestNoAliveTiFlashRetry`, `TestTiFlashPartitionTableShuffledHashAggregation`, `TestTiFlashPartitionTableBroadcastJoin`, `TestTiFlashPartitionTableShuffledHashJoin`, `TestTiFlashPartitionTableReader`, `TestTiflashSupportStaleRead`, `TestTiflashPartitionTableScan`, `TestStoreErr`, `TestStoreSwitchPeer`, `TestDisaggregatedTiFlash`, `TestDisaggregatedTiFlashNonAutoScaler`, `TestTiFlashComputeDispatchPolicy`, `TestDisaggregatedTiFlashQuery`, `TestDisaggregatedTiFlashGeneratedColumn`, the MPP dispatch and batch-cop arms of the server's `TestTiFlashFallback`, the enforcempp casetest `TestMPPMultiDistinct3Stage`, and the physicalplantest casetests `TestMPPBCJModel`, `TestMPPPreferBCJ` and `TestMPPBCJModelOneTiFlash`; `unistore_cop/mpp_execution.rs`). A disaggregated TiFlash builds its tasks as Go's `buildBatchCopTasksConsistentHash` and `buildBatchCopTasksConsistentHashForPD` do (`batch_cop_tasks.rs`: the AutoScaler's or PD's alive tiflash_compute nodes, the round-robin and rendezvous-hash policies, per physical table). Partitioned reads are Go's too (the generator's `partitionPruning`, per-partition task building and `TableRegions`, a union scan's buffer read; `TestReadPartitionTable`, `TestTiflashEmptyDynamicPruneResult`). TiFlash late materialization is Go's (`tiflash_predicate_push_down.rs`: the scan's pushed down filter, its `lm_col_scan` cost and `PushedDownFilterConditions`). Left: a TiFlash scan's `UsedColumnarIndexes` (vector, inverted and full-text indexes, with the inverted-index arm of `handleTiFlashPredicatePushDown`), the MPP CTE operators (CTE sink and source with their `ToPB`, the generator's CTE task counts and `fillLocalCTECounts`), the local index lookup in `ToPB` and the store (`indexLookUpExec`), and the single-fragment lowering (`mpp_coordinator.rs` `open_mpp_scan`) a TiFlash read over a transaction's buffer still takes. A non-MPP TiFlash read is Go's batch-cop or cop (`batch_coprocessor.rs`: `batchCopIterator`, its retry over rebuilt tasks, the peer switch of `OnSendFailForBatchRegions`, the cancel cause; the embedded store's `BatchCoprocessor`; a TiFlash request's empty resource group while resource control is off), and its task build's warnings reach the statement (`TransportRequest`'s `AppendWarning`), short of the batch task's exec info and the `tiflash_replica_read` zone warning of `buildTableReader`. A dispatch or establish follows Go's retry contract (`MppRpcError`'s `retry`, the coordinator's loops, `needTriggerFallback`), a failed dispatch runs `OnSendFailForBatchRegions` over its task's regions, the planner's `preferMppBCJ` reads `GetMPPStoreCount`, and a root response is charged to the statement while it waits for the gather (`sendToRespCh`); the store's receive failpoints fire where the embedded store collects a task's packets. A gather's error is recovered as Go's `ExecutorWithRetry` does over `RecoveryHandler` (`recovery_handler.rs`: the held responses, three recoveries, the memory-limit handler of an auto-scaled cluster), and a batch task's stores are checked alive as Go's `checkAliveStore` does (copr `TestAliveStoreSkipCheck`, `TestCheckAliveStore`).

SQL/PB signature construction. Go's `functionClass.getFunction` returns one signature object that carries the wrapped arguments, the return type, the `PbCode` and the evaluation. Here every name in Go's `funcs` map has its function class (`builtin::funcs`), `new_function` is the only builder, and the cast, `getvar` (with `convertReadonlyVarToConst`), `values`, `to_binary` / `from_binary` builders are Go's (`BuildCastFunction`, `BuildGetVarFunction`, `NewValuesFunc`, `BuildToBinaryFunction`, `BuildFromBinaryFunction`); the classes are compared with Go's `NewFunction` in `tidb-expr/testdata/function_class_matrix.txt` and `cast_class_matrix.txt`. What is still not one object: the class returns the arguments, the type, the `PbCode` and the evaluation (a kernel on `BaseBuiltinFunc`), the decoder binds the same kernels and `PbConverter` (`expr_to_pb.rs`) sends the node's own signature, type and arguments -- every request condition, aggregate argument and key goes through it; but `extensionFuncs` holds an arity, not an `extensionFuncClass`: `pkg/extension` (`FunctionDef`, the manifest that registers one) is not ported and nothing registers a function. Go's alternative-plan rounds are the planner driver's (`planner_optimized_query_with_allocators`, Go `optimize`): under `tidb_opt_enable_alternative_logical_plans` the first round's signals arm Go's seven rounds in Go's order (`ALTERNATIVE_ROUNDS`: non-decorrelate, order-aware-reorder, correlate with `CorrelateSolver`, semi-join-rewrite, fts-like-fallback, tikv-only, tiflash-only), each round rebuilds from the restored build context (`LogicalPlanBuildState`, plan and column ids, scalar subqueries) and the cheapest plan is the statement's, pinned by Go's `correlate_suite_out.json` and a Go testkit capture (`tidb-session/testdata/alternative_rounds_go.json`); a native-viable `MATCH` competes with the ILIKE plan on cost. One plan differs on purpose: under costly joins Go's correlate round turns `a in (select a from t2 limit 5)` into an Apply over `TableDual rows:0` and returns no rows; here the cloned scan stays and the rows are right (the capture leaves that case out). A `FOR UPDATE` read in an explicit transaction keeps its paths in the builder and marks `MissingTiFlashPath` (Go `isForUpdateReadInExplicitTxn`), `findBestTask4LogicalDataSource` filters them, the fast plan is tried only with TiKV among the engines, and a point get is a cost-compared candidate before the storage hint skips its path -- pinned by a Go testkit capture over a TiFlash replica (`tidb-session/testdata/for_update_read_tiflash_go.txt`). The engine-restricted rounds pick the plans of Go's `TestAlternativeEngineRestrictedRounds` (`casetest/mpp/testdata/integration_suite_out.json`, over hypothetical TiFlash replicas). `fts_match_word` is Go's in the starter deployment: the class marks `FTSFunctionIsUsed`, `FTSResolveIndex` (`rule_fts_resolve_index.rs`) binds it to the table's full-text index and the TiFlash scan carries it, pinned by Go's `TestTiFlashFTSMatchWordPushDown`, `TestTiFlashFTSMatchWordPreparedPlanCache`, `TestTiFlashFTSMatchWordDirtyTxn` and `TestFTSRequiresStarterMode`; a table's `FULLTEXT` keys pass Go's `buildFullTextInfoWithCheck` and `checkColumnarIndexIfNeedTiFlashReplica` (`tidb-session/testdata/fts_create_table_go.txt`, a Go testkit capture) and `SHOW CREATE TABLE` prints the three columnar kinds as Go does.

No lazy InfoSchema V2, schema-cache-size loader/evictor or InfoCache timestamp ranges; `ReportMinStartTS` reads the InfoCache's recent-schema TS (`GetAndResetRecentInfoSchemaTS`), which nothing lowers because no V2 reader calls `keepAlive`
BRIE statements are classified but never executed

On a bound node every DDL statement over `mysql.tidb_ddl_job`, `tidb_mdl_info` and `tidb_ddl_reorg` runs Go's SQL on a session of `DdlSessionPool::sess_pool` or the step's session (the systable `Manager`, the scheduler's `loadAndDeliverJobs`, `SwitchMDL`, the submission insert, a step's update / delete / history insert, the reorg handle's reads and writes, `UpdateConfigFromSysTbl`, `runOneJobStep`'s job-cancelled checker, `GetAllDDLJobs` and `get2JobsFromTable`). What remains: a pool no node has bound (the store-level harness and the bootstrap) keeps the snapshot twin of each read (`SnapshotSystemTables`) and stages raw job rows, where Go's DDL always has its session pool; a step reads its job row inside its own transaction (`DdlJobTable::load_by_id` in `cluster_ddl.rs`) where Go's `deliveryJob` refreshes the delivered job by `sysTblMgr.GetJobByID` between steps; accounts load eagerly where Go loads per active user (the site-by-site list is the retired `docs/system-table-sql-execplan.md`, in git at `d64db1f96bc`)

Go's `ExecRestrictedSQL` / `ExecuteInternal` are methods of the issuing session (`withRestrictedSQLExecutor`); this port's executors are adapters beside it (`NodeRestrictedSql`, `SystemSqlExecutor`, `ClusterStatsSqlExecutor`, the plan replayer's `SessionSql`). The node's executors apply and restore `ExecOption` as Go's `useCurrentSession` / `getInternalSession` do, and share a `RestrictedSqlIssuer` with the session they were taken from, through which the internal session inherits `OptimizerUseInvisibleIndexes` / `SkipMissingPartitionStats` and hands its warnings back (`IgnoreWarning`); the statistics session's executor is the same pair (`ClusterStatsSessionState::restricted`), and an ANALYZE is an auto analyze because its session is `InRestrictedSQL`. The internal session is a pooled one's (`getSessionFactoryInternal`: its own autocommit, max_execution_time, max_allowed_packet and in-place constraint check, and no copy of the global tier) and shares the issuer's `InspectionTableCache`. What remains: a user session's executor cannot run a statement on the session itself (`ExecOptionUseCurSession`). `rebuildSysVarCache` consumes the rows the domain's sysvar reload loop last read (`SysVarCacheDeps::table_contents`) where Go's runs `fetchTableValues` itself
